slides.title: Tire Repairing, Inflation and Mounting
slides.description:
Tire Repairing, Inflation and Mounting

Tire repairing, inflation and mounting are dangerous activities. Shop employees can be killed from tire explosions-not to mention those who have suffered serious injuries or whose hearing has been seriously impaired.

slides.title: Tire Repairing, Inflation and Mounting cont’d
slides.description:
Hennessy Industries (La Vergne, TN) has summed up tire safety in one word-RIM. R-read, I-inspect and M-mount.

Readthe tire and wheel to make sure they are the same size. A 16-inch tire an a 16.5-inch wheel (or vice versa) can cause an explosion.

Inspect the wheel for rust, bent flanges or cracks that could cause problems and inspect the tire for damage.the wheel for rust, bent flanges or cracks that could cause problems and inspect the tire for damage.

Mountthe tire safely. Never stand over the tire while you are inflating it. Never inflate a tire beyond its rated pressure to seat the bead. If you have to do this, something else is wrong. Deflate and check the tire and rim again.

slides.title: Additional Tips
slides.description:
Do not inflate tire in poor condition-a blowout could occur. Examples of a tire in poor condition include a damaged tread, cut sidewall or one that is bald.

Keep yourself on one side of the tire when checking or inflating it-never directly in front of the tire.

Each tire-inflation hose should have a snap-on chuck with at least 24 inches of hose between the chuck and the in-line valve and gauge. The air should shut off when the valve is released.

Keep hands and fingers away from pinch points.

If a tire is suspect of having a defect, deflate the tire before dismounting from the vehicle.

Lifting a tire improperly is a potential back-safety hazard. Lift with legs from the squatting position. Be careful when rolling tires around as they can easily get out of control and cause an accident.

slides.title: Slip-Rim or Locking-Ring Wheels
slides.description:
Heavy trucks and equipment have two-piece rims. Inflating these tires can be extremely dangerous. The rim may fly off during inflation. Follow these safety rules tips:

Use a tire-restraining device, such as a cage, chain or other means, when inflation tires mounted on split rims or rims using retainer rings.

Use a clamp-on connector with an in-line pressure gauge to connect the air hose to the tire stem. You can then inflate the tire out of the immediate danger area.
